meta.title: cc-orchestra: one project, two editions
meta.description: cc-orchestra comes in two editions. cc-orch runs coding and research work on a Linux server with Claude Code and Codex CLI; cc-doc is a document desk on Windows 11. This page introduces both and links to each.

hero.h1: One harness for code, one desk for documents.
hero.lede: cc-orchestra comes in two editions, each named after its command. cc-orch splits a coding request into tasks and connects Claude Code and Codex CLI across planning, implementation and verification, on a Linux server. cc-doc opens one Claude Code session for document work on Windows 11, where a single desk agent works on copies.

editions.p: Each edition has its own platform, its own way of working and its own pages on this site.

cards.name: cc-orch
cards.title: For coding and research work
cards.text: An orchestrator splits your request into tasks and a lead owns each one. In the default mode, Codex writes the code, the Claude lead reads the real diff, and separate Codex gates verify and review the result.
fits: You work on code or run research projects on a Linux server.
You run several tasks at once, need checks you can rely on, or work on something that spans weeks.

pages.text: One researcher's paper workflow, run as tasks.
What it is and when it is worth using.

cards.name: cc-doc
cards.title: For document work
cards.text: One Claude Code session with a single desk agent for Hangul, Word and PowerPoint documents. It works on copies in a work folder made for that session and returns results under a name that is not yet in use. A write guard checks the paths that Claude Code's file-writing tools and tool-server calls name and refuses those outside that folder, within documented limits.
fits: You write Hangul, Word or PowerPoint documents on Windows 11.
You want your originals left where they are while the work happens on copies.

pages.text: The desk, copies, the write guard and document types.
